[0] Earlier reports indicated that Apple plans to launch a 20th-anniversary edition iPhone next year, featuring an all-glass body design. However, analysts at investment bank Jefferies believe the device will not move forward.

[1] Wall Street analysts say the major redesign of the 20th-anniversary iPhone has been shelved.

[2] Wall Street investment bank Jefferies has downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today. Analyst Edison Lee noted that the potential cancellation of the major redesign for the 20th-anniversary iPhone is one of the main reasons for this downgrade.

[3] The key to this downgrade lies in news that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been cancelled. Although rumours about this project being under development surfaced as early as 2025, with some expecting a 2027 launch, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent for an "all-glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies previously considered an all-glass iPhone reasonable and credible, but Edison Lee believes development has stalled. The analyst noted that supply chain checks indicate the project was terminated due to poor yield rates. Edison Lee believes that with memory costs soaring, this decision is a "major blow" to driving high-end iPhone sales. He estimated that if the device launched in September 2027 as planned to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, its average retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average price of any previous model. Edison Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe Apple originally planned to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, thereby further raising average selling prices and gross margins." He believes that with memory prices rising, this should have been an important defensive strategy.

[4] Edison Lee also pointed out that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are other reasons for this stock downgrade.

[5] Based on Edison Lee's report, it remains unclear whether the analyst is referring to the entire redesign plan being shelved, or only some design elements being abandoned.

[6] The most-liked comment was posted by Currentinterest.

[7] These analysts have been wrong too many times about Apple's future plans. Even the concept of an "all-glass" design has never accurately reflected Apple's true intentions. The 20th-anniversary phone will be unique and creative, and whatever the final design turns out to be, it will be hugely popular.

[8] For example, reports circulating for months have pointed out that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an all-glass display is simply impossible. However, the rumoured four-curved-edge bezel design may still be achievable.

[9] In any case, if the redesign of the 20th-anniversary iPhone has indeed been cancelled, credible media outlets should confirm this news very soon.
